item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Pat McAfee did not enjoy his time at the University of Utah this weekend as the school hosted ESPN’s College GameDay ahead of the No. 10 Utes showdown with No. 14 Houston. On Monday, both ESPN and the university responded to what turned into a larger-than-expected drama with statements regarding the matter. During the final segment of Saturday’s show in which the hosts pick the home game they’re broadcasting from, McAfee voiced several frustrations he had with the weekend at Utah before going on to pick Houston to win on the road. McAfee cited a video shared across the university’s social channels before the broadcast, in which some students made jokes about him sometimes employing a corny line while making his picks and taking his shirt off as a bit to rile up the crowd. He also referenced the student who was chosen to partake in his kicking contest, who balked at the offering of $1 million for the kick, noting that the prize the previous weekend at BYU was $3 million. The video, which likely would have gone mostly unnoticed if not for McAfee raising attention to it, has since been deleted from Utah’s social channels, but as with everything else anyone tries to delete from the internet, lives on elsewhere. item.title: Was This the Best Rivalry Weekend Ever for the Minnesota Golden Gophers
item.description: There is no doubt it was an incredible weekend to be a fan of the Minnesota Golden Gophers. The Gopher football team did enough and picked up their first home win over Iowa since 2014 to keep Floyd in Minneapolis. After two weekends of absolutely dreadful hockey the Gopher men’s hockey team figured something out in a hurry and not only swept but dominated #3 North Dakota in a series at 3M Arena at Mariucci. The Gopher women outscored Lindenwood by a total score of 16-2 on the weekend including 11 goals in the opening game and a program record 73 shots on goal in the second game of the series against the Lions. The Gopher Volleyball team picked up a 3-0 sweep of #21 Washington. The Gopher soccer team closed out the home portion of their schedule with a 1-1 tie against #12 Washington and a dominant 4-0 win over Oregon at Elizabeth Lyle Robbie Stadium. It is hard to do much better. In fact, when looking specifically at rivalry matchups we would argue that we never have done better. At least for rivalry purposes was the best weekend in Minnesota Golden Gopher athletics!* (We will put a caveat that a better term might be the modern era of Golden Gopher athletics. Is it possible there was a better rivalry weekend in the 1940’s—it’s possible, but it gets a lot harder to sort thrugh those university records) So why do we say that? Well, first we took a look at every single weekend where the Gopher football team won one of the Big Three trophy games—sorry Penn State, just don’t have the same feel. So after we looked at every single weekend going back to the 1960’s where the Gophers won either Paul Bunyan’s Axe, Floyd of Rosedale, or the Little Brown Jug, we then looked at any other major matchups from that weekend—either Gopher hockey or Gopher men’s basketball. Admittedly, unless you get into some of the games where Minnesota won these trophies late in November, there are not many basketball games to add to this equation. Also, back in the 1960’s and 197’s the Gopher hockey season didn’t really start until late October either which is also a limiting factor. After looking at the football winning weekends, we looked at hockey and basketball weekends. Were there some weekends where yes the Gopher hockey team went 2-0 in a trophy winning weekend—you bet. Were several of these weekend sweeps of Alaska Anchorage or other non-impressive weekends. Yes. Were there also a surprising number of weekends where the Gopher football team won a trophy and the Gopher hockey team was playing North Dakota—-also yes. In fact, including this past weekend was the third time in the last six seasons that the Gopher football team had won a trophy game and the men’s hockey team was facing off against the Fighting Hawks. item.title: How White Sox Can Trade Luis Castillo for an Elite Pitching Upgrade
item.description: Sep 22, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Chicago White Sox pitcher Luis Castillo (58) pitches during the ninth inning against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Purnell-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Chicago White Sox front office is currently in a difficult position as they have to decide what to do about Luis Castillo. The situation looks difficult, as Castillo was acquired at the trade deadline to add experience to the pitching staff and guide an emerging young rotation in the postseason; instead, the 33-year-old posted an 8.42 ERA across the final stretch of Chicago’s 2026 regular season and was demoted to the bullpen before landing on the injured list. He was not part of the roster for the postseason, as Will Venable doesn’t seem to trust him, and the Sox are likely not going to be depending on him next season. ‎So, what should be the best move for the White Sox concerning Castillo? Castillo has one more year of control entering 2027, and it’s not cheap. The White Sox owe him $24 million, and there’s a vesting option for $25 million for 2028 that vests with 180 innings pitched in 2027. The conventional move for White Sox would be to hope for a Spring Training bounce-back. The analytical move would be to eat 50% to 60% of his remaining salary in a trade and reallocate the saved money to upgrade the pitching staff by getting top-of-the-rotation starters. Should Chicago take the conventional move, they carry a huge financial burden and a player who will turn 34 next year and is likely to produce worse performance. Why the White Sox Cannot Afford To Have Luis Castillo on the 2027 Roster Luis Castillo was one of the best starting pitchers in the league in the early 2020’s. In fact, from 2020 to 2023, he posted an average 3.44 ERA in over 600 innings, which by any standard is top-level production. But he began to decline in 2024, posting a 3.64 ERA, and in 2025, a 3.54 ERA. Before the White Sox acquired him, he had a 5.06 ERA in 2026. What led to his significant decline was that his successful four-seam fastball velocity dropped, and his Vertical Approach Angle (VAA) flattened out and became inconsistent. A flat VAA reduces pitching velocity while increasing barrel-rate contact from the batter. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Le-Imagn Images ‎Also, Castillo’s WHIP increased to 1.49 in 2026 from 1.16 in 2024. What led to that was that his two-strike fastballs plummeted from 28.5% to 22%, while his strikeout rate took a downward swing from 24.3 % to 18.9%. Should Castillo remain on the White Sox roster in 2026, his value is expected to be around 0.2 WAR, and in current baseball economics, 1 WAR is valued between $8 million and $9 million. item.description: Steve Stone and John Schriffen posed before their first regular season game together, on March 28, 2024. Believe it or not, this awkward photo represented the high point of Schriffen’s White Sox career. | (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) October 26, 2005, is a date that will forever live in the hearts of White Sox fans. An out-of-nowhere, 99-win juggernaut ended an 88-year World Series drought. Now, 21 years later, a shorter but still ignominious era ended not with a bang, but a soft rawr . The entirely-predictable has finally happened, as the White Sox play-by-play broadcaster John Schriffen’s contract was not extended by the White Sox, and 2026 will be the last of perhaps the strangest three-year stretch in White Sox broadcasting history. There will be many of Schriffen’s defenders putting out their lamentations at the quick and seemingly unfair ending to a young broadcaster’s career in Chicago. This, however, will not be one of them. Schriffen was perhaps the worst broadcaster not only in White Sox history, but perhaps in all of MLB annals. Now of course, there’s no comparing him to men who threw their careers away with a flippant or careless slur … as Castellanos hits a drive into left-field for a home run. That will make it a 4-0 game … but Schriffen is going out in a way that seems somewhat quaint and old-fashioned in today’s viral cancellation climate. He was just bad at his job. Looking back, John came into this role at the worst and lowest point in this franchise’s history. The 2020-21 championship window had shut as quickly as it had been open. The 2023 team had just wrapped up the first of three consecutive 100+ loss seasons. So naturally, Jerry Reinsdorf decided that uber-talented, multi-network PBP man across multiple sports and Chicagoland native White Sox fan Jason Benetti was just taking too much of Jerry’s precious airtime doing Friday Night Baseball on Apple or Sunday Nights on ESPN and let Jason out of his contract early…ONLY FOR HIM TO IMMEDIATELY BE HIRED BY THE GO**AMNED DETROIT TIGERS ( who, ironically, just extended Benetti’s contract at the end of the 2026 season ). item.title: Exclusive: Rob Gronkowski on Tom Brady support in broadcasting career
item.description: Exclusive: Rob Gronkowski on Tom Brady support in broadcasting career appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . From Super Bowl wins to broadcast mics, the brotherhood between Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady did not leave the football field. Gronk exclusively revealed to ClutchPoints last month how they have been supportive of one another as they navigate their new broadcasting careers. “I mean, we’ve helped each other by just making each other feel comfortable,” Gronkowski said in ClutchPoints’ interview via his partnership with Bounty. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite having different roles on air — Gronk is a studio analyst for FOX NFL Sunday, and Brady is a lead NFL color analyst at FOX Sports — adding that Brady has a “whole different preparation” from him, they are still there to support one another. “But what makes us feel good about it is that we know that we’re there for each other if anything. Sometimes segments running to each other, we roll into each other and it’s always great, people love it,” he added. “The connection that we have at Fox coming from the football field is just phenomenal.” Brady and Gronk were teammates on two teams during their careers in the NFL. The pair first played together on the New England Patriots for nine seasons — 2010 through 2018 — where they were able to win three Super Bowls together (Super Bowl 2014, 2016, and 2018). The tight end then came out of retirement to join Brady to play for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for two seasons — 2020 and 2021). They would win their last Super Bowl together in the 2020 NFL season. Gronk also showed love to Julian Edelman who was their Patriots teammate at the time and is now an analyst on Fox NFL Kickoff. “Also, Julian Edelman being there as well on the pregame show we help each other,” Gronk continued. “[We] feel very, very comfortable because we’ve been teammates in the past and now we’re teammates in the future as well, which is what makes it like super, super special.” Brady signed a 10-year, $375 million contract with FOX Sports to serve as the network’s lead NFL color commentator in May 2022. Edelman joined FOX Sports in 2023. Gronk signed his first contract with FOX Sports in 2019 and came back in 2022 as an NFL analyst after retiring for a second time. In 2025, Gronk landed his full-time, weekly role on FOX NFL Sunday to replace Jimmy Johnson. item.title: ‘They Were Bullied’ — Super Bowl Champion Sounds Alarm on Chiefs for Getting ‘Out-Physicaled’ by Seahawks
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker (7) reacts after missing a field goal against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field. © Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Seattle Seahawks made a statement on Sunday night as they look to repeat as Super Bowl champions. Seattle took down the Kansas City Chiefs, who were undefeated and one of the top teams in the AFC, in convincing fashion on Sunday Night Football. The way the Seahawks shut down a high-powered Kansas City offense (albeit one missing more than a few names) turned a few heads, with Super Bowl champion WR Greg Jennings among those expressing concern about the Chiefs’ outlook for the rest of the season. Greg Jennings Dampens His Expectations for the Chiefs The Chiefs were completely outmatched for the first time in the 2026 season as the Seahawks rolled to a statement victory after not having the best start to the season themselves. Kansas City’s offense dominated all defenses they faced through Week 6, but Seattle proved to be a force they couldn’t overcome. Jennings was particularly concerned with Kansas City’s inability to match the physicality that Seattle played with. “They were just flat-out dominated. They were bullied. They were out-physicaled,” Jennings said on “First Things First.” The Chiefs don’t have to panic, because they are off to such a great start. Mahomes looks back to his normal self with his ability to move after his ACL tear, and Kenneth Walker III has been one of the best running backs in the NFL so far. Walker is the top-ranked back in PFN’s RB Impact score with a grade of 94.1, but the Seahawks limited their former star to just 36 yards after tallying at least 117 rushing yards in four of his first five games. Mario Hezonja's return to the NBA could prove to be critical for the Cavaliers, who are looking for any edge possible as they try to keep up with the East's improved rosters. Hezonja, a former lottery pick of the Magic , spent six years out of the NBA before a stint with Real Madrid that included an MVP put him on the radar of front offices once again. Why Mario Hezonja could be NBA's most underrated offseason signing Hezonja was a role player for just about all of his first five seasons with the Magic, so what does he bring a title-hopeful Cavaliers team? With Cleveland's core in place and unchanged, they aren't looking for him to be any kind of hero. Hezonja's veteran leadership is already making a difference. Facing the Nets on Saturday, he took the bold step of waving off Donovan Mitchell in the third quarter and explained his logic after the game. "I told him [Mitchell] you're not supposed to bring the ball up under pressure because we need you in the last quarter," Hezonja told reporters. "We need you in the playoffs. We need you in game 80, game 60. Having somebody like me that can help. As I said on the first day, I'm here to help you." Hezonja said it's "beneficial" any time he can take some of the pressure off the Cavaliers' stars, and that way of thinking could make a major difference as Cleveland tries to fine-tune its operation. Hezonja appears to be a more fearless, hardened player after finding success in Spain, and he showcased his value as a rebounder with five boards in less than 20 minutes against Brooklyn. For just $2.85 million, what Hezonja can offer the Cavaliers team that needed help around the margins might make him a bargain. item.title: Kendal Daniels goes from being carted off field to saving Falcons’ season
item.description: Kendal Daniels goes from being carted off field to saving Falcons’ season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels experienced one of the most remarkable turnarounds of the NFL season, going from being carted off the field on a stretcher to delivering a game-changing performance just seven days later. Daniels recorded 11 tackles, an interception and a fumble recovery in Atlanta’s 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The victory improved Atlanta’s record to 3-4 while handing San Francisco its first loss of the season. Just one week earlier, Daniels suffered a frightening neck injury against the Chicago Bears that required medical personnel to immobilize him before transporting him to Grady Hospital. However, the rookie returned to practice Wednesday and was cleared to play against San Francisco. “It’s been the craziest week of my life,” Daniels told ESPN . “I’ve never not walked off the field after an injury.” Daniels delivered his biggest play with Atlanta protecting a 26-20 fourth-quarter lead. With approximately three minutes remaining, Daniels intercepted quarterback Brock Purdy and returned the football 29 yards, setting up Nick Folk’s 31-yard field goal. He later recovered a fumble forced by safety Jessie Bates III, officially ending San Francisco’s comeback hopes. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski praised the rookie’s resilience following the victory. “That’s remarkable, truly,” Stefanski said. “What a great kid. We just gave him a game ball, and he deserves it because what a week.” Daniels also handled defensive communication responsibilities with veteran linebacker Divine Deablo sidelined by a forearm injury. His performance highlighted an Atlanta defense that forced four turnovers against one of the NFL’s strongest teams. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. contributed three touchdown passes and 213 passing yards in the victory. For Atlanta, the win snapped a two-game losing streak and provided much-needed momentum heading into an important NFC South matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . For Daniels, Sunday’s performance represented something even greater: an inspiring comeback that his teammates will remember throughout the season. item.title: Brandon Artis steps down as Evansville Central football coach
item.description: EVANSVILLE — Brandon Artis has stepped down as the Central High School football coach. He confirmed the resignation to the Courier & Press after it was listed during Monday night's Evansville Vanderburgh School Corp. board meeting. Artis went 3-37 with the Bears across four seasons, the longest tenure for a head coach in the program since Andy Owen retired in 2017. Following a winless campaign in 2023, Artis guided the Bears to a single victory each of the last three seasons. Central finished 1-9 this fall following a loss to Bedford North Lawrence in the first round of the Class 4A sectional. More: What we learned from first round of IHSAA football sectional in Southwestern Indiana Artis, a 2007 graduate, was a football and track standout with the Bears before earning a degree in exercise science at Indiana State University. He coached both sports at multiple schools, including three years as the head coach of the Memorial girls track & field program. Artis is also stepping down as a physical education teacher per the EVSC board meeting agenda, effective Nov. 13. Central averaged 17.3 points per game this season, a team best under Artis, but ranked last in the Southern Indiana Athletic Conference at 54.4 points allowed per game. Six opponents scored more than 50 points, including the final two games against North and BNL. The Bears lose their top passer, rusher, multiple receivers and multiple top tacklers to graduation. The program isn't too far removed from the best stretch in school history. Central won three sectional championships in a four-year period and advanced to the state title game in 2018. The Bears only have five wins across the last six seasons under two coaches. This story will be updated. Kyle Sokeland is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo. Cam Skattebo’s reward for running through the Houston Texans’ defense was a comparison to Mike Tyson. It did, however, come with a warning about how long the Giants running back can maintain his punishing style. NFL analyst Colin Cowherd loved what Skattebo brought to Sunday’s win. The second-year back had gone without a touch in Week 6 after fumbling against the Washington Commanders the previous week. Skattebo felt he had been punished for the mistake, but head coach John Harbaugh denied benching him. Sunday’s performance gave the running back a chance to put the controversy behind him and prove his value to the Giants. Cowherd was impressed by Skattebo’s physicality, but he questioned how long the running back could keep playing that way. Colin Cowherd Compares Cam Skattebo to Young Mike Tyson Skattebo rushed for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries in New York’s 27-21 overtime victory over the Texans. His 42-yard run in overtime helped set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning touchdown and gave the Giants a much-needed glimpse of what their backfield can provide when Skattebo is at his best. Cowherd praised Skattebo’s performance on Monday’s edition of “The Herd,” pointing to the running back’s ability to create missed tackles and help open up the Giants’ passing game. “Cam Skattebo fumbled against Washington. They should have won that game. And John Harbaugh benched him. But now we’re playing Houston, 7.2 yards a carry, the Texans are a very good tackling defense, and he forced eight missed tackles. And more importantly, it allowed J.J. McCarthy to throw on play action,” Cowherd began.
